investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-28T02:32–02:33Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint at /v1/agents was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs before any agent identity is returned, zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were collected, causing a complete contract violation for all sibling checks.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" on every attempt. Because the failure happens at the very first network hop (POST /api/agents → swarm gateway), no agent is created and no evidence can be collected, causing all three remote-agents checks to fail with the same message. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: image-generation-stream eval failure: OpenAI API credit balance exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to return a hard error (code: credit_balance_exhausted). The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, so both contract assertions — frameTypes containing "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equaling true — were violated. This is an eval infrastructure / API credential issue, not a product code defect, and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The OpenAI organization account whose API key is used by the eval runner at /api/generate/image/stream has exhausted its credit balance. The API returned HTTP error type "insufficient_quota" with code "credit_balance_exhausted" before image generation could complete. As a result, the SSE stream emitted a generation_error frame instead of generation_completed, imageUrlPresent was never set to true, and both required contract assertions failed. The AURA application routing and stream-framing code are not implicated; the failure originates at the external API billing boundary.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returns 502/424 provider_account_unavailable
investigations.summary: The model-matrix eval check failed because exactly one of two configured models, aura-gpt-5-5, returned a 502 Bad Gateway wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable. The other model, aura-claude-sonnet-4-6, passed cleanly. This is a localized eval failure against the aura-gpt-5-5 model route; no sibling checks failed and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: AURA's backend was temporarily unable to reach the upstream provider for model aura-gpt-5-5 at the time of the eval run (2026-08-28T02:32:13Z). The runtime test endpoint POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned HTTP 502 containing a nested 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable and the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." This caused the model result to record ok: false, provider: null, resolvedModel: null, which in turn caused the allPassed and failedModelCount assertions in the model-matrix expected-output contract to fail. The aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 (Anthropic) model was unaffected, indicating the disruption is specific to the provider backing aura-gpt-5-5 rather than a broad platform outage.

Lower probability: A routing or model-resolution failure within AURA's runtime harness specific to aura-gpt-5-5 that prevents provider resolution (evidenced by resolvedModel: null and provider: null in the result), which could indicate the model was not resolved before the provider call was attempted.

investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. If the GitHub Actions workflow run history shows a successful publish run completed within the past 300 minutes at the time of the eval, it would suggest a GitHub Pages caching or propagation delay rather than a missed workflow run.

If the published status.json generatedAt timestamp, when fetched directly, is within 300 minutes of the eval run time (2026-08-28T02:33:22Z), it would indicate the snapshotAgeMinutes calculation in the runner is incorrect rather than the snapshot being genuinely stale.
If the source field in a fresh fetch of status.json shows 'github-actions' with a recent generatedAt, it would confirm the automated workflow is running and the prior failure was a one-time gap.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that checks the GitHub Actions workflow run recency directly (e.g., last successful run of the snapshot publish workflow within the past 300 minutes) to catch workflow scheduling failures before they cause snapshot staleness.
Add a warning-level eval threshold at snapshotAgeMinutes > 180 (3 hours) to provide earlier signal before the hard failure at 300 minutes.

Add an eval assertion that source equals 'github-actions' specifically, or at minimum alerts when source is 'desktop-nightly-release' for more than one consecutive run, to detect when the automated publish pipeline has silently stopped contributing.
Add a GitHub Pages deployment recency check to detect propagation delays between a successful workflow run and the live published file being updated.
